content:
Once upon a time, in a small neglected town, there lived a slim girl named Mira. Mira came from a very poor family, where every meal was a luxury, and dreams of simple pleasures were often out of reach. But Mira had an unusual wish: she longed to be fat. To her, being larger meant comfort, abundance, and a life far from hunger.

Desperate to change her fate, Mira applied for a job as a waitress at a local restaurant. The place was run down, the food was bad, and the patrons were few. Mira convinced the restaurant owner to let her stay there rent-free in exchange for helping out when needed. She also asked him if she could eat the leftover food after closing time, promising she wouldn’t ask for wages.

The owner agreed; after all, he was eager for any help and had plenty of leftovers because of the poor quality of his meals.

Days turned into weeks, and Mira ate every leftover morsel she could find. As she gained weight, she felt joy she had never known. She finally felt full, safe, and nurtured. But with every passing day, she grew larger — so large that one day, she found herself unable to squeeze through the restaurant’s doors anymore.

Now trapped inside, Mira could no longer leave or even use the restroom properly. The restaurant became her entire world, and sadly, without proper hygiene or care, she began to live in her own filth.

The unpleasant conditions, in turn, drove away the few customers who had remained loyal. The restaurant’s reputation declined, and the owner faced bankruptcy.

Eventually, the restaurant shut its doors for good, abandoned and empty — except for Mira, who remained alone inside, a quiet reminder of a dream turned into a lonely, tragic reality. 

Her story spread as a cautionary tale about the dangers of desires left unchecked, and about how sometimes, wishes come at a cost far greater than anyone ever imagines.
